title: Bribing an inserted coordinate
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $J$ be a finite set of indices in $\\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, let $i$ be such an index, and let $b\in\{-1,1\}$. For every sign vector $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$, replacing the coordinates in $J\cup\{i\}$ by $b$ gives the same vector as first setting coordinate $i$ of $x$ to $b$ and then replacing the coordinates in $J$ by $b$.
hypotheses_covered: $J$ is a finite set of indices in $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$
$x$ is a sign vector of length $n$
